messages.subject: Syntax for formative constructs
parts:
Dear lavaan community, 

At the moment, I am working on testing my second order model. The goodness of fit for model appears to be good (n = 168; CFI = .978; TLI = .975; RMSEA = .028; SRMR = .059)

Model Test User Model:
                                               Standard      Robust
  Test Statistic                                240.947     227.373
  Degrees of freedom                                201         201
  P-value (Chi-square)                            0.028       0.098
  Scaling correction factor                                   1.060

Overall_model<-'
                ELDIR =~ ELDIR2 + ELDIR4 + ELDIR5 + ELDIR7 + ELDIR8
                ELDIR7 ~~ ELDIR8
                ELDIP =~ ELDIP1 + ELDIP2 + ELDIP3 + ELDIP4 + ELDIP6  
                SNFER=~ SNFER1 + SNFER2 + SNFER3 + SNFER4 + SNFER5
                                SNFER1 ~~ SNFER2
                SNFEC =~ SNFEC1 + SNFEC2  + SNFEC4
                SNFEA =~ SNFEA2 + SNFEA3 + SNFEA4Rev+ SNFEA5

                ELDI =~ ELDIR + ELDIP
                SNFE =~ SNFER + SNFEC + SNFEA
                ELDI ~ SNFE'

model1<-sem(Overall_model, data=data,  estimator="MLR", missing="FIML")
summary(model1, fit.measures=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

However, as the author of one research instrument for ELDIR and ELDIP does not provide enough information, I have second thoughts that his instrument might be of a formative nature (i.e. All items imply on different actions and might not be considered interchangeable). The author reports his usage of AMOS while I have read that this software cannot properly handle formative constructs. Therefore, I am searching for options to adjust my syntax for using the constructs of ELDIR and ELDIP as formative ones. The goal is to understand whether both factors should be used as formative or reflective.

Before writing, I have read all threads about formative constructs; however, since I am new to lavaan, I have not found them to be useful. Apart from the operator "<~" that doed not seem to work, I have not found anything useful; therefore, I would appreciate any comments or suggestions. 

Many thanks in advance. 

Regards, 
Artem

messages.subject: Re: Syntax for formative constructs
parts:
Hello again. 

Since I have not received any reply to date, I will try to wave my hand as an attempt to get some attention. Also, I will try to make some clarifications to my initial question. 

My goal was and is to run the analysis for testing the factors that I believe are supposed to be used as the formative ones. I believe that there has been misspecification in some papers while the constructs were used as the reflective ones. Before considering this, I have spent some time while learning on theoretical considerations and following the guidelines of Roberts and Tharcher (2009), I believe that the indicators I want to test have a formative nature. In the same paper, it was described that if there is a formative factors that has indicators and is used as dependent variable, the PLS method should be adapted. 

However, as I am using lavaan, I am wondering whether it is possible to make the factors ELDIR and ELDIP formative and how could I do that? 
Here is the model with all reflective constructs. 

Mediation_model<-'

ELDIR =~ ELDIR2 + ELDIR4 + ELDIR5 + ELDIR7 + ELDIR8
                                ELDIR7 ~~ ELDIR8
                ELDIP =~ ELDIP1 + ELDIP2 + ELDIP3 + ELDIP4 + ELDIP6  

                SNFER=~ SNFER1 + SNFER2 + SNFER3 + SNFER4 + SNFER5
                                SNFER1 ~~ SNFER2
                SNFEC =~ SNFEC1 + SNFEC2  + SNFEC4
                SNFEA =~ SNFEA2 + SNFEA3 + SNFEA4Rev+ SNFEA5

CTW=~ CTW1 + CTW3 + CTW4 + CTW5 + CTW7 + CTW8
                                CTW1 ~~ CTW3

ELDI =~ ELDIR + ELDIP
                SNFE =~ SNFER + SNFEC + SNFEA

#structural model
                ELDI ~ a*SNFE
                CTW ~ c*SNFE + b*ELDI

#Test of Indirect Effects
                ind:=a*b
                total := a*b + c'

Med_model<-sem(Mediation_model, data=data,  estimator="MLR", missing="FIML")
summary(Med_model, fit.measures=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)

I would appreciate any ideas and comments on how to make this work in R. 

I apologise if my question still sounds stupid but as a novice researcher I have some concerns in regard to the constructs I am using. Therefore, I would be glad for any suggestions and assistance while using lavaan. 

Regards, 
Artem

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Syntax for formative constructs
parts:
> However, as I am using lavaan, I am wondering whether it is possible to
> make the factors ELDIR and ELDIP formative and how could I do that?

Syntax-wise, you need to change '=~' (reflective) by '<~' (formative).
If this works, then you are done. If not, you may have identification
issues. I am not familiar enough with formative constructs to guide you
here; you will have to consult the literature.

Yves.

Perhaps this is done automatically (not sure), but I would fix the scale
as follows:

ELDIR <~ 1*ELDIR2 + ELDIR4 + ELDIR5 + ELDIR7 + ELDIR8
ELDIP <~ 1*ELDIP1 + ELDIP2 + ELDIP3 + ELDIP4 + ELDIP6

>                 ELDIR ~ a*SNFE
>                 ELDIP ~ d*SNFE

This two lines look strange to me: SNFE is now just another 'indicator'
of the formative constructs ELDIR/ELDIP
>                 WTC ~ c*SNFE + b*ELDIR + e*ELDIP

Yes, this is what need (I think): ELDIR/ELDIP must be predictors in an
regression equation.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Syntax for formative constructs
parts:
In your diagram, you can see that 'ELDIP' has incoming arrows from its
indicators (ELDIP1, ELDIP2, ...) but also from SNFE.

If you wish to allow for residual error, you may prefer the following
syntax:

ELDIP =~ 0 # create a phantom latent variables
ELDIP ~~ ELDIP # free residual error
ELDIP ~ ELDIP1 + ELDIP2 + ELDIP3 + ELDIP4 + ELDIP6

ELDIP ~ SNFE

(and the same for ELDIR)

This will allow for EDLIP to have (residual) variance. Clearly, this
syntax also shows that SNFE is just another 'predictor' of ELDIP.

Yves.
